purpose: Does a transformer behaviorally garbage-collect overwritten facts? Two binary registers, 32 roots (8 per final store in {0,1}^2), 4 literal actions, normalized {0,1} task-aligned observer. Tests idempotence, absorption, commutation, erasure. Codex Architecture Theorist design (2026-09-04).

key_design_choices: Two binary registers, not variable scoping
4 literal actions identical for every root (no variable substitution)
Task-aligned {0,1} observer as primary, full-vocab as diagnostic
32 roots with 8 per final store for erasure convergence testing
Genuine algebraic relations: idempotence, absorption, commutation
Fix CRC-0 bugs: cross-fitted closure, non-oracle NN baseline

algebraic_relations.idempotence: a=v; a=v should equal a=v alone (same future behavior)
algebraic_relations.absorption: a=u; a=v should equal a=v alone (earlier write is dead)
algebraic_relations.commutation: a=u; b=v should equal b=v; a=u (independent registers commute)

pass: >= 95% algebraic relation satisfaction on held-out roots
Compact transition table within 0.01 TV of uncompressed at <= 1/4 states
fail: Dead histories remain visible (overwritten writes change future behavior)
